record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: Can the Caccetta-Haggkvist conjecture be verified for fixed small values of the minimum out-degree k, beginning with the currently first unsettled case k = 6?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1 Verify Conjecture 3.1 for small values of k starting from k = 6.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture asserts that every finite simple digraph on n vertices in which every vertex has out-degree at least n/k contains a directed cycle of length at most k. Equivalently, for every integer k ≥ 1, if D is a digraph on n vertices with minimum out-degree at least ⌈n/k⌉, then D contains a directed cycle of length at most k.

The conjecture is known to hold for k ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. The problem is to settle the conjecture for the next fixed value, k = 6: prove or disprove that every digraph on n vertices with minimum out-degree at least ⌈n/6⌉ contains a directed cycle of length at most 6. More generally, settle the conjecture for further fixed small values of k beyond k = 6.
artifact.status_search_result: The Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture has been proved for k = 1, 2, 3 (Hamidoune) and k = 4, 5 (Hoàng–Reed), and for all sufficiently large k (k ≥ 224,539 via Shen-type bounds). The case k = 6 is the first unsettled fixed small case and does not appear to have been resolved in the literature; the standard open-problem repositories continue to list it as open.

status_evidence.title: Caccetta-Häggkvist Conjecture | Open Problem Garden
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture was proved for r=2, for r=3 by Hamidoune, and for r=4 and r=5 by Hoàng and Reed.
status_evidence.claim: Original conjecture is established only up to k=5, with k=6 the next open case.

status_evidence.title: Caccetta-Häggkvist Conjecture (West)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem page listing partial results for small r; r=6 not listed among solved cases.
status_evidence.claim: k=6 case of Caccetta–Häggkvist remains open.
